knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $s=\sin\left(51^\circ\right)$ and $c=\cos\left(51^\circ\right)$. The **double-angle formula** gives $\sin\left(102^\circ\right)=2sc$.

 Also, $\tan\left(51^\circ\right)=\frac{s}{c}$.

Rewrite the quotient ratio before cancelling.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2sc}{\frac{s}{c}} &=2c^2 \\ &=2\cos^2\left(51^\circ\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

All cancellations use nonzero factors in the original expression.

generation.domain: Original denominators and reciprocal functions must be defined; sampled angles are acute and nonspecial.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $s=\sin\left(47^\circ\right)$ and $c=\cos\left(47^\circ\right)$. The **double-angle formula** gives $\sin\left(94^\circ\right)=2sc$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2sc}{2s} &=c \\ &=\cos\left(47^\circ\right)
